change.description: Add the administrator AI usage operations surface, per-user quota controls, and a dashboard view covering the latest seven natural days with timezone-aware stacked usage totals and success, failure, cancellation, missing, and estimated usage visibility.
change.release_unit_description: static frontend and full-feature Docker image

planned.reasoning: The admin-only operations surface adds compatible read and same-origin policy endpoints plus UI routes. It does not remove existing routes, alter public response shapes, or add durable state schema changes.

evidence.command: REQ-SKA-018 requires the dashboard to show seven natural days, a consistent timezone, input/cache/output/call metrics, and incomplete usage visibility; review follow-up requires failure and cancelled call visibility
The admin API adds an additive dashboard usage read route while retaining the existing protected admin boundary

current.reasoning: The candidate adds the admin AI usage page, user quota operations, shared usage client types, and the dashboard seven-day usage panel. The dashboard endpoint reuses the existing service aggregation and returns only timezone, range, metric, and trend data; the dashboard now exposes success, failure, cancelled, missing, and estimated call states without database migration or durable state shape changes.

evidence.command: Dashboard renders four AI usage cards, a three-band seven-day stack, an exact-value table, timezone labeling, and success, failure, cancelled, missing, and estimated call counts
Dashboard usage is an additive protected GET route backed by the existing seven-day AI usage aggregation
The Web Demo mock exposes the dashboard route with deterministic Asia/Shanghai seven-day data and empty/dense data modes

scope_drift.description: The change remains within the T5 administrator operations surface, its protected API contract, deterministic Web Demo fixtures, and focused verification; public site behavior, database schema, and provider metering semantics remain out of scope.

verified.reasoning: The protected dashboard API contract passes the HTTP compatibility test, the compiled admin build succeeds, and the Web Demo passes desktop and mobile acceptance for the new dashboard surface plus the existing AI usage and user quota flows. The dashboard shows all seven natural-day rows, timezone labeling, additive token dimensions, and success, failure, cancelled, missing, and estimated status without introducing persistent state changes.
